summary: Specifies additional example methods for generating Key Identifier values for the AKI and SKI certificate extensions. The methods are examples, and this is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo adds four example ways to generate key identifiers for certificate extensions. Three use truncated hashes of the public key, and one hashes the encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

questions: how does rfc 7093 generate key identifiers
subtitle: Additional example methods for generating X.509 certificate key identifiers.

tldr.problem: RFC 5280 gives examples for generating AKI and SKI values, and this memo adds further methods.
tldr.mechanism: It describes truncated SHA-256, SHA-384, and SHA-512 hashes of the subjectPublicKey value, plus hashing the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo.
tldr.outcome: The RFC provides additional examples for key identifier generation; it notes that hash resistance properties are not needed for key identifiers.

today: RFC 7093 is an Informational document with additional example methods for generating certificate key identifiers. The unit metadata lists no update or replacement.

sections.title: Key Identifiers in Certificates
sections.content:
RFC 5280 defines the Authority Key Identifier and Subject Key Identifier certificate extensions and gives two example generation mechanisms based on SHA-1. RFC 7093 adds four more example mechanisms.

Three use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 on the subjectPublicKey bit string. The fourth hashes the DER encoding of the SubjectPublicKeyInfo value.
sections.plainLanguage: Certificates can include identifiers for the authority's key and the subject's key. This memo adds ways to calculate those identifiers.

sections.title: Four Additional Generation Methods
sections.content:
The first three methods use the leftmost 160 bits of the SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 hash of the subjectPublicKey bit string. The RFC specifies which part of the bit string is hashed, excluding its tag, length, and number of unused bits.

The fourth method hashes the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo value. The memo does not specify a single hash algorithm for that method.
sections.plainLanguage: Three methods take the first 160 bits of a hash of the key data. Another method hashes the encoded structure that contains the key information.

sections.title: Examples and Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC provides hexadecimal examples using a DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo value containing a P-256 ECDSA key. It shows hashes of the public-key bytes and of the complete encoded value.

The security considerations of RFC 5280 and RFC 5758 apply. The RFC notes that preimage, second-preimage, and collision resistance are not needed for key identifiers.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples show concrete hash values so implementers can check calculations. The memo says key identifiers do not require the listed hash-resistance properties.

references.text: Cooper, D., Santesson, S., Farrell, S., Boeyen, S., Housley, R., and W. Polk, "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile", RFC 5280, May 2008.
Dang, Q., Santesson, S., Moriarty, K., Brown, D., and T. Polk, "Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure: Additional Algorithms and Identifiers for DSA and ECDSA", RFC 5758, January 2010.
